text:
Anika Patel: heads up — customer ACME reported decrypt failures after we rotated their CMK this morning. they can encrypt but decrypt -> AccessDenied from their app.
Dinesh Rao: did they use cross-account grants or key policy changes during rotation?
Anika Patel: looks like cross-account. their service account in account B was granted access via a grant we created last month. rotation flow used alias swap + new key.
Sam Voss: can you paste the exact error and any request IDs?
Anika Patel: error from our API logs -> \"Decrypt operation failed: AccessDeniedException\". aws request id: 9f4e2c3a-1d7b-4e2f-a9b7-2b0c7b8f9c3a. app log shows: \`ClientError: An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the Decrypt operation\`.
Support Ops: customer also pasted aws cli test: 
```
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ciphertext.bin --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-1234 --encryption-context Application=acme,Env=prod
```
response: AccessDeniedException
Dinesh Rao: two common causes: 1) grant wasn't re-created for new key after alias swap 2) encryption context mismatch (we enforce context in decrypt). which policy/grant path did they use?
Anika Patel: they used a Grant from account A to account B principal `arn:aws:iam::210987654321:role/acme-service-role`. The grant ARN is `arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:grant/7a8b9c`. Grant shows `Operations: Encrypt,Decrypt,ReEncryptFrom`.
Sam Voss: if grant references key id of old key it won't work after alias swap unless grant targets the new key id. alias swap flow we do is: create new key -> re-encrypt prefixes -> update alias -> schedule old key for pending deletion. Grants don't automatically move.
Anika Patel: customer insists we told them rotation is transparent. they expected alias swap to preserve grants.
Dinesh Rao: for cross-account opens, we usually recreate grants as part of rotation runbook. check if our rotation automation skipped grant copy when key creation had tagging mismatch.
Support Ops: I pulled rotation run log: `rotation-job-2026-03-10-03` shows step `copy-grants` returned 0 grants copied due to `PrincipalMismatch` tag filter.
Anika Patel: aha — they had a custom tag `team:acme` on the old key but new key didn't include that tag because automation filtered tags.
Sam Voss: that matches. if the automation's grant-copy step filters by tag and tags differ, grants are not recreated. fix options: 1) recreate grant manually for their principal on new key, 2) update automation to copy tags before grant copy so copy succeeds, 3) allow alias pointing to old key for now (not ideal).
Dinesh Rao: immediate remediation: create a grant on new key for their principal with same constraints (encryption context enforced). commands: 
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id <new-key-id> --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::210987654321:role/acme-service-role --operations Decrypt Encrypt ReEncryptFrom --constraints EncryptionContextSubset={\"Application\":\"acme\",\"Env\":\"prod\"}
```
replace `<new-key-id>` with `arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/efgh-5678`
Anika Patel: ran that for customer and asked them to retry. they reported success: decrypt returned plaintext. :tada:
AWS-KMS-Bot: Note: grant `g-0a1b2c3d4e5f` created for key `efgh-5678` by `Anika Patel` at 2026-03-10T08:24:12Z.
Support Ops: closing loop — told customer the root cause and next steps. also opened internal ticket to update rotation job to copy tags and/or not filter on tags. ticket: RDW-ENG-5123.
Sam Voss: please add a short blurb to runbook: ensure `copy-grants` step runs after tags are synced, and include commands to recreate grants.
Dinesh Rao: also add a check to rotation CI: validate grant count on new key equals old key. fail otherwise.
Anika Patel: will write runbook patch and link customer comms.
Support Ops: customer asked if encryption-context is required — we confirmed it's recommended and if enforced then decrypt requires matching subset. sent link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-cross-account (internal runbook)
Anika Patel: marking thread resolved. thanks all.
